The **2011–12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team** was a historic squad that made program history by earning the school's first-ever **NCAA Tournament** berth (since the Ivy League began awarding an automatic bid in 1953). Coached by **Tommy Amaker**, the Crimson finished with a **26–5** record (12–2 in Ivy League play), winning their second consecutive Ivy League title and becoming the first team in league history to clinch an NCAA bid without a playoff.

### **Key Highlights of the 2011–12 Season:**
#### **1. Historic NCAA Tournament Berth**
- Harvard earned the **Ivy League’s automatic bid** by finishing **12–2 in conference play**, two games ahead of second-place Yale.
- This was the first time Harvard (or any Ivy League team) **avoided a playoff** for the NCAA bid under the league’s then-current format (the Ivy League did not have a postseason tournament until 2017).
- The Crimson received a **No. 12 seed** in the **East Region**, facing **No. 5 Vanderbilt** in the first round (more on that below).

#### **2. Regular Season Success**
- **26–5 overall record** (a program best at the time, later surpassed by the 2014–15 team’s 27 wins).
- **Undefeated at home (11–0)** at Lavietes Pavilion.
- **Non-conference wins**:
  - Beat **Florida State (65–66 in OT, at the Battle 4 Atlantis)** – a major upset over a future ACC champion.
  - Defeated **St. John’s (74–67)** in New York.
  - Took **UConn (then defending national champs) to OT** before falling 67–53 at the **Battle 4 Atlantis** (Harvard led late in regulation).
- **Ivy League dominance**:
  - Swept **Princeton** and **Yale** (two of their biggest rivals).
  - Only losses came at **Penn (70–69)** and **Yale (69–58)**.

#### **3. NCAA Tournament Run**
- **First Round (March 15, 2012)**: **No. 12 Harvard vs. No. 5 Vanderbilt** (in Albuquerque, NM).
  - Harvard led for much of the game, including a **13-point halftime lead (42–29)**.
  - Vanderbilt stormed back in the second half, but **Laurent Rivard** hit a **game-tying three with 11 seconds left** to force OT.
  - In overtime, Harvard **outscored Vandy 8–5** to win **72–69**, pulling off one of the biggest upsets of the tournament.
    - **Key performers**:
      - **Laurent Rivard** (22 pts, 6/9 3PT)
      - ** 오랜楚 (Keith Wright)** (16 pts, 8 reb)
      - **Brandyn Curry** (12 pts, 5 ast)
  - This was **Harvard’s first ever NCAA Tournament win** (they had been 0–2 previously, in 1946 and 2010).
- **Second Round (March 17, 2012)**: **No. 12 Harvard vs. No. 4 Wisconsin**
  - The Crimson **fell 72–65** to the Badgers, ending their season.
  - **Keith Wright** led Harvard with **18 points and 7 rebounds**.

#### **4. Key Players**
Harvard had a **balanced, experienced roster** with multiple All-Ivy performers:
- **Keith Wright (Sr., F/C)** – **Ivy League Player of the Year** (unanimous)
  - Averaged **14.8 PPG, 8.5 RPG, 1.8 BPG**
  - First Crimson player to win Ivy POY since **Jeremy Lin (2010)**.
- **Brandyn Curry (Jr., G)** – **First-Team All-Ivy**
  - **12.3 PPG, 5.1 APG, 4.4 RPG** (team leader in assists)
  - Clutch performer in big games.
- **Laurent Rivard (So., G/F)** – **Breakout star**
  - **14.6 PPG, 4.2 RPG**, shot **44.6% from three** (one of the best shooters in the country).
  - Hit **6 threes** in the win over Vanderbilt.
- **Kyle Casey (Jr., F)** – **First-Team All-Ivy**
  - **11.4 PPG, 6.7 RPG**, versatile scorer and defender.
- **Christian Webster (Jr., G)** – **Key sixth man**
  - **9.3 PPG**, provided scoring off the bench.
- **Jonah Travis (Fr., F)** – **Ivy League Rookie of the Year**
  - **7.6 PPG, 5.1 RPG** in limited minutes, showing promise for the future.

#### **5. Coaching & System**
- **Tommy Amaker** (5th season at Harvard) was named **Ivy League Coach of the Year**.
  - Built a **defensive-minded, disciplined** program that valued ball movement and three-point shooting.
  - This season cemented Harvard as a **legitimate mid-major powerhouse** (they would reach the NCAA Tournament **four times in a row** from 2012–15).
- **Style of Play**:
  - **Efficient offense**: Harvard ranked **15th nationally in field goal percentage (48.9%)**.
  - **Strong defense**: Held opponents to **63.3 PPG** (top 50 nationally).
  - **Three-point shooting**: Rivard, Curry, and Webster were all **38%+ shooters from deep**.

#### **6. Legacy & Impact**
- **Broke Harvard’s NCAA Tournament drought** (first appearance since **1946**, first win ever).
- **Proved Ivy League basketball could compete nationally** – their win over Vanderbilt was a **program-defining moment**.
- **Laid the foundation for future success**:
  - The 2012–13 team would return **most of its core** (minus Wright) and make the **NCAAs again** (as a **No. 14 seed**, nearly upsetting New Mexico).
  - Harvard became a **consistent Ivy League champion** under Amaker, making the **NCAAs in 2012, 2013, 2014, and 2015**.
- **NBA & Pro Careers**:
  - **Keith Wright** played briefly in the **NBA (Sacramento Kings, 2012 summer league)** and had a long career overseas.
  - **Brandyn Curry** played professionally in Europe.
  - **Laurent Rivard** had a brief stint in the **NBA G League** before playing overseas.

#### **7. Notable Games & Stats**
| Opponent | Result | Key Notes |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| @ Florida State | **W 66–65 (OT)** | Firstever win over an ACC team on their home court. |
| vs. UConn | L 67–53 (OT) | Tough loss to eventual national champs at Battle 4 Atlantis. |
| vs. St. John’s | **W 74–67** | Big non-conference road win. |
| @ Penn | L 70–69 | One of only two Ivy losses. |
| vs. Princeton (x2) | **W 61–58, W 60–59** | Swept their biggest rival. |
| **NCAA Tournament: vs. Vanderbilt** | **W 72–69 (OT)** | **First NCAA win in program history.** |
| **NCAA Tournament: vs. Wisconsin** | L 72–65 | Season ended in Round of 32. |

- **Team Stats (2011–12)**:
  - **PPG**: 72.3 (98th nationally)
  - **Opponent PPG**: 63.3 (48th nationally)
  - **FG%**: 48.9% (15th nationally)
  - **3PT%**: 38.9% (25th nationally)
  - **Rebound Margin**: +5.1 (33rd nationally)

#### **8. Ivy League & National Recognition**
- **Final KenPom Ranking**: **#75** (highest in program history at the time).
- **Final AP Poll**: Received **votes** (not ranked, but close).
- **Ivy League Awards**:
  - **Player of the Year**: Keith Wright
  - **Coach of the Year**: Tommy Amaker
  - **Rookie of the Year**: Jonah Travis
  - **First-Team All-Ivy**: Wright, Curry, Rivard, Casey
  - **Second-Team All-Ivy**: Christian Webster

#### **9. Where Are They Now?**
- **Tommy Amaker**: Currently the **head coach at Harvard** (as of 2024), though he had a brief stint as an assistant with the **Boston Celtics (2022–23)**.
- **Keith Wright**: **Director of Player Development** for the **Harvard men’s basketball team** (2021–present).
- **Laurent Rivard**: Played professionally in **Europe (France, Germany, Belgium)** before retiring.
- **Brandyn Curry**: Works in **real estate** after a pro career in Europe.
- **Kyle Casey**: Played overseas (Germany, Japan) before transitioning to **coaching** (assistant at **Amherst College**).

### **Conclusion**
The **2011–12 Harvard Crimson** were a **groundbreaking team** that put Harvard basketball on the map nationally. Their **NCAA Tournament win over Vanderbilt** remains one of the most memorable moments in Ivy League basketball history, and their success helped **legitimize the league** as a source of competitive, well-coached teams. Under Amaker, Harvard became a **model mid-major program**, combining **academic excellence with athletic success**.
